summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status until April 2029, overriding any other law.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires designation of Haiti for temporary protected status but contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It has no bearing on government spending levels.
The bill addresses immigration status designation only and includes no tax-related measures, rate changes, or revenue provisions.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare policy, coverage, or market structures.
The legislation is unrelated to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Homeland Security designate Haiti for temporary protected status (TPS) through a specific future date. TPS grants eligible nationals of designated countries protection from removal and work authorization, directly expanding immigration protections and pathways for Haitians.
